obligation.description: When a leader releases admitted remote ReadIndex requests upon quorum confirmation in a stable term and membership, each response to a released request origin must preserve that request full SystemCtx so its origin can associate readiness with the admitted operation, including requests released as a prefix by confirmation of a later context.

scope.description: Per-peer ReadIndex response correlation for distinct remote origins with one pending request each; stable multi-voter term and membership, current-term committed entry, valid nonzero distinct contexts and generated quorum confirmation.
assumptions: Crash-fault message loss may discard earlier heartbeats while later heartbeats and responses are delivered.
Peer caller persists exported entries/state before dependent outbound messages, applies committed configuration in order, and acknowledges updates.
Each origin has exactly one admitted request so origin independently identifies its expected response.
excluded: No claim of stale application values, global infinite stalling, numeric latency bound, or client RequestState completion.
No restarts, membership transitions, context reuse or fabricated peer messages.

grounding.derivation: TestReadIndexLeaderCanBeConfirmed explicitly requires each released status to retain its own context even when confirmed as a prefix; TestHandleFollowerReadIndexResp requires emitted response context to become readiness context unchanged. The actual pendingReadIndex.addReady consumer indexes batches by the full SystemCtx, so origin identity plus a later unrelated context cannot discharge the earlier admitted request. The obligation is local preservation across the remote response boundary, not a guarantee that all reads succeed or meet a deadline.
grounding.applicability: Distinct remote origins, one pending request per origin, stable term and membership, legal quorum release of a queued prefix.
alternatives: Confirm raises earlier indices to the later index deliberately; index equality with the original index is not required.
Client timeout can bound a lost operation but does not repair an already-emitted response identity.
